rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-idḥāḍ literally means making someone slip; here it metaphorically means defeat and loss.
rows.anchor: والإدحاض : جعل المرء داحضا ، أي زالقا غير ثابتت الرجلين وهو هنا استعارة للخسران والمغلوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-iltqām means swallowing; the fish was enormous, swallowed objects without biting, and was reportedly called al-bālīn in European usage.
rows.anchor: والالتقام : البلع . والحوت الذي التقمه : حوت عظيم يبتلع الأشياء ولا يعض بأسنانه ويقال : إنه الحوت الذي يسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mulīm is the active participle of alāma: Jonah did what made people blame him, making himself blameworthy.
rows.anchor: والمليم : اسم فاعل من ألام ، إذا فعل ما يلومه عليه الناس لأنه جعلهم لائمين فهو ألامهم على نفسه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The author locates Jonah’s drowning in the Sea of Rome, the Mediterranean, and rejects some exegetes’ claim that it was the Tigris.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن بنهر دجلة كما غلط فيه بعض المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being among the glorifiers refers to Jonah’s prayer in 21:87; God rescued him because of his glorification and repentance.
rows.anchor: فأنجاه الله بسبب تسبيحه وتوبته فقذفه الحوت من بطنه إلى البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives three nights in the fish, while also recording alternatives of one day and night or a few hours.
rows.anchor: بعد أن مكث في جوف الحوت ثلاث ليال ، وقيل : يوما وليلة ، وقيل : بضع ساعات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported duration for Jonah’s stay in the fish is one day and one night.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يوما وليلة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported duration for Jonah’s stay in the fish is a few hours.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بضع ساعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means indefinitely: God may have caused the fish to die after swallowing Jonah, leaving both at the sea bottom until resurrection.
rows.anchor: بأن يميت الله الحوت حين ابتلاعه ويبقيهما في قعر البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, a fish could have been trapped in something underwater and never surfaced, so Jonah would remain on the seabed until resurrection.
rows.anchor: أو بأن يختطف الحوت في حجر في البحر أو نحوه فلا يطفو على الماء حتى يبعث يونس يوم القيامة من قعر البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in the following passage is explanatory, supplying the omitted account that Jonah prayed in the fish, God answered and rescued him.
rows.anchor: فالتقدير : يسبح ربه في بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish expelled Jonah, disgorging him, and the waves carried him to shore.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : فلفظه الحوت وقاءه ، وحمله الموج إلى الشاطىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabdh means casting or throwing; its attribution to God reflects that He subjected the fish to cast Jonah onto the shore.
rows.anchor: والنبذ : الإلقاء وأسند نبذه إلى الله لأن الله هو الذي سخر الحوت لقذفه من بطنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿarāʾ is ground without trees or anything that covers it.
rows.anchor: والعراء : الأرض التي لا شجر فيها ولا ما يغطيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah emerged ill because the fish’s intestines moving around him damaged his skin; he had removed his clothes before being thrown into the sea to swim more easily.
rows.anchor: وكان يونس قد خرج من بطن الحوت سقيما لأن أمعاء الحوت أضرت بجلده بحركتها حوله فإنه كان قد نزع ثيابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author conjectures that God made the fish nearly faint, partly suspending digestion so its intestines would not harm Jonah’s flesh.
rows.anchor: ولعل الله أصاب الحوت بشبه الإغماء فتعطلت حركة هضمه تعطلا ما فبقي كالخدر لئلا تضر أمعاؤه لحم يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqṭīn is a squash plant with abundant leaves that climbs onto elevated objects; its branches likely covered and shaded Jonah’s body.
rows.anchor: أغصان اليقطينة تسلقت على جسد يونس فكسته وأظلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Squash was chosen so Jonah could eat its produce and recover, a divine kindness following the hardship of his discipline.
rows.anchor: واختير له اليقطين ليمكن له أن يقتات من غلته فيصلح جسده لطفا من ربه به بعد أن أجرى له حادثا لتأديبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative ‘that’ refers to the loss and punishment just described.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما وصف من الخسران والعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takhwīf is making someone afraid by showing or describing something that can cause pain through one of the senses.
rows.anchor: والتخويف : مصدر خوفه ، إذا جعله خائفا إذا أراه ووصف له شيئا يثير في نفسه الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine possessive ‘servants’ in both occurrences addresses all people, believers and unbelievers, since all fear punishment; its severity ranges up to the polytheists’ everlasting punishment.
rows.anchor: العباد المضاف إلى ضمير الجلالة في الموضعين هنا يعم كل عبد من الناس من مؤمن وكافر إذ الجميع يخافون العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ‘servants’ does not mean God’s close elect: that would not suit the warning, and the address to all servants confirms the broader sense, unlike 43:68.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يناسب مقام التخويف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God follows the threat because warning implies punishment is prepared for the disobedient, making taqwā the fitting next instruction.
rows.anchor: فناسب أن يعقب بأمر الناس بالتقوى للتفادي من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative precedes the consequent command to focus attention in this warning context; in 2:197, pilgrimage exhortation instead places the command before the vocative and joins it with wāw.
rows.anchor: لأن المقام هنا مقام تحذير وترهيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ of the first-person suffix is deleted in ‘yā ʿibād’ according to one of five possible forms for a vocative annexed to that suffix.
rows.anchor: على أحد وجوه خمسة في المنادى المضاف إلى ياء المتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After threatening polytheists and admonishing everyone, the discourse turns to believers’ good news, in contrast to the warning; the clause signals why they merit it and answers 39:16.
rows.anchor: لما انتهى تهديد المشركين وموعظة الخلائق أجمعين ثني عنان الخطاب إلى جانب المؤمنين فيما يختص بهم من البشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author analyzes ṭāghūt as a verbal or deverbal noun from ṭaghā on the pattern faʿalūt, like raḥamūt and malakūt; the root’s final weak letter has both wāw and yāʾ forms.
rows.anchor: والطاغوت : مصدر أو اسم مصدر طغا على وزن فعلوت بتحريك العين

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs appears to favor a wāw in the root form; the following pattern-wāw makes the final weak letter heavy, prompting metathesis and the form ṭāghūt, with tāʾ added for intensification.
rows.anchor: وإذ كانت لامه حرف علة ووقعت بعدها واو زنة فعلوت استثقلت الضمة عليها

rows.speaker: من العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars treat ṭāghūt as a foreign word on the pattern fāʿūl; al-Itqān says it means ‘soothsayer’ in Abyssinian, and Ibn Ḥajar added it to Ibn al-Subkī’s list of Quranic loanwords.
rows.anchor: وذكره في ( الإتقان ) فيما وقع في القرآن من المعرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Quran and Sunna, ṭāghūt denotes a powerful force in unbelief or oppression: an idol, a group of idols, or a leader of unbelievers such as Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf; here it means idols collectively.
rows.anchor: وأطلق الطاغوت في القرآن والسنة على القوي في الكفر أو الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ṭawāghīt reflects predominance of its nominal use, though a single idol is an uncommon referent; feminine ‘worship them’ treats it as a nonrational plural.
rows.anchor: وأما جمعه على طواغيت فذلك على تغليب الاسمية علما بالغلبة إذ جعل الطاغوت لواحد الأصنام وهو قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun for ṭāghūt agrees with its sense as a nonrational plural; 2:257 uses masculine agreement because it is predicated of masculine plural ‘allies’ or treated as rational by its worshippers.
rows.anchor: وباعتبار تنزيلها منزلة العقلاء في زعم عبادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause ‘that they worship them’ is a بدل اشتمال (inclusive apposition) of ṭāghūt.
rows.anchor: و { أن يعبدوها } بدل من { الطاغوت } بدل اشتمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ināba means repentance, as at 11:75; here it means repenting from every sin, above all from the pre-Islamic shirk they practiced.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها هنا التوبة من كل ذنب ومعصية وأعلاها التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bushrā means good news; here it is the good news of Paradise, as in the phrase about good news in this life and the next at 10:64.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها هنا : البشرى بالجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preposing ‘for them’ in ‘for them is the good news’ conveys restriction, paralleling the restrictive clauses in 39:18.
rows.anchor: إفادة القصر وهو مثل القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good-news command refers to those who avoided ṭāghūt; replacing ‘announce to them’ with ‘announce to My servants’ and a relative clause adds praise for devotion to God and hearing and following the best speech.
rows.anchor: إلى الإظهار باسم العباد مضاف إلى ضمير الله تعالى

rows.speaker: العشرة ما عدا السوسي
rows.claim: All ten readers except al-Sūsī read ʿibādi with kasra on dāl and no yāʾ, a lightening that relies on the kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العشرة ما عدا السوسي راوي أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: السوسي
rows.claim: Al-Sūsī reads a yāʾ after dāl, open in connected reading and silent at pause; deletion at pause is also reported and both forms are grammatical, though the codices omit the yāʾ, weakening the reading unless treated as performance.
rows.anchor: وقرأها السوسي بياء بعد الدال مفتوحة في الوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite ‘speech’ is generic: it includes guidance such as the Quran and the Messenger’s instruction, as well as misguiding fabrications; they follow what is best, which calls to truth.
rows.anchor: أي يستمعون الأقوال مما يدعو إلى الهدى مثل القرآن وإرشاد الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥsan here does not rank one good saying above another; it intensifies the quality, as in Joseph’s ‘prison is dearer’ at 12:33.
rows.anchor: فاسم التفضيل هنا ليس مستعملا في تفاوت الموصوف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God praises them as discerning guidance from error, wisdom from illusions, and real proofs from sophistry; following the best speech points toward their receiving God’s guidance.
rows.anchor: أثنى الله عليهم بأنهم أهل نقد يميزون بين الهدى والضلال والحكمة والأوهام نظار في الأدلة الحقيقية نقاد للأدلة السفسطائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause is a fresh sentence that draws attention; the demonstrative singles out the people and highlights their deserving divine care because of the qualities just listed.
rows.anchor: مستأنفة لاسترعاء الذهن لتلقي هذا الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic discourse uses a demonstrative after descriptions to emphasize a judgment: it may point to the subject, as here, or to the predicate, as in 38:55.
rows.anchor: والإتيان باسم الإشارة عقب ذكر أوصاف أو أخبار طريقة عربية في الاهتمام بالحكم والمحكوم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defining both parts restricts guidance to them in an specifying, additional sense, as distinct from those who lost themselves and their families.
rows.anchor: وهو قصر إضافي قصر تعيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s guidance means He created souls receptive to the Prophet’s guidance; they wholeheartedly listened and sought His approval and rescue from wrath, rather than merely receiving commands available to all.
rows.anchor: بأن خلق الله نفوسهم قابلة للهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s guidance here does not mean simply directing guidance commands to them, since those who ignored the Quran also received that address.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد بهدي الله إياهم أنه وجه إليهم أوامر إرشاده لأن ذلك حاصل للذين خوطبوا بالقرآن فأعرضوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause attributes receptivity to God-given, sound intellects naturally inclined to truth over custom and falsehood; people differ in how quickly they reach guidance, with Khadīja, Abū Bakr, and ʿAlī believing at the first call.
rows.anchor: بما فطرهم الله عليه من عقول كاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separating pronoun, possessive ‘people of,’ definite ‘intellects,’ and repeated demonstrative signal fully rooted understanding and distinguish them; ‘intellects’ is not generic because all rational people have some.
rows.anchor: فليس التعريف فيه تعريف الجنس لأن جنس الألباب ثابت لجميع العقلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance requires an agent and a recipient: God is the agent, while the people of intellect are receptive; the second clause carries the same restriction as the first.
rows.anchor: تنبيه على أن حصول الهداية لا بد له من فاعل وقابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise for following the best speech honors inquiry and argument that distinguish truth from falsehood and right from error, close off doubt, and expose sophistry.
rows.anchor: على شرف النظر والاستدلال للتفرقة بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reasoning needed to acquire sound belief is an individual duty, measured by each person’s capacity; deeper inquiry into Islamic law, its proofs and purposes, and sound social practice is a collective duty and excellence.
rows.anchor: واجب على الأعيان وهو ما يكتسب به الإعتقاد الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Collective inquiry includes fiqh and understanding objectives in worship, transactions, and social etiquette, sustaining the Muslim community and answering deceivers, extremists, and heretics.
rows.anchor: والفقه في ذلك والفهم فيه والتهمم برعاية مقاصده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This principle calls for selecting the soundest proofs and most effective arguments without flaw by refining the sciences and their books; one should take the best from each science.
rows.anchor: بدون اختلال ولا اعتلال بتهذيب العلوم ومؤلفاتها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A saying applies the verse as an instruction to take the best from every field of knowledge.
rows.anchor: قيل : خذوا من كل علم أحسنه أخذا

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verses were revealed about Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Abū Dharr, and Salmān, who avoided idol worship in pre-Islamic times and followed the best teaching that reached them.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن زيد نزلت في زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وأبي ذر الغفاري وسلمان الفارسي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the good-news passage was revealed about ʿUthmān, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Ṭalḥa, al-Zubayr, Saʿīd ibn Zayd, and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, who came to Abū Bakr after his conversion, heard his testimony, and believed.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس نزل قوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restrictions on good news, guidance, and understanding imply that polytheists lack the good end because they lack obedience; an emphatic rhetorical question then warns that the condemned group cannot be expected to find guidance.
rows.anchor: فرع على ذلك استفهام إنكاري مفيد التنبيه على انتفاء الطماعية في هداية الفريق الذي حقت عليه كلمة العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse confirms a good group’s description by asserting its opposite for the opposite group, so the proposition is established twice; 38:49 and 38:55 illustrate the pattern, which follows a demonstrative here.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء نظم الكلام على طريقة مبتكرة في الخبر المهتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ suitably derives this sentence from the preceding declaration that the other group is guided and people of understanding; Labīd similarly derives one simile from another because their comparisons differ.
rows.anchor: وبهذا يظهر حسن موقع الفاء لتفريع هذه الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites Labīd’s couplet about a wild cow and its guide as an example of deriving one comparison from another.
rows.anchor: كالتفريع في قول لبيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿadhāb means God’s threat of punishment in the afterlife, and ḥaqqa means that the threatened word has become real and is no lie.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { حق } تحققت في الواقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned group’s having the punishment fixed and being in the Fire oppose the others’ guidance and good news, arranged as a reversed distribution; 2:6–7 follows 2:4–5 similarly.
rows.anchor: وترتيب المتضادين جرى على طريقة شبه اللف والنشر المعكوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers’ hearts soften on hearing mercy after the fear raised by warnings; softness metaphorically means acceptance and joy, as opposed to the hardness condemned in 39:22.
rows.anchor: واللين : مستعار للقبول والسرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After warnings make believers fear and avoid what is forbidden, promises make them rejoice, recognize promised good in their deeds, and turn fear into hopeful expectation.
rows.anchor: فإذا عقب ذلك بآيات البشارة والوعد استبشر وفرح وعرض أعماله على تلك الآيات فرأى نفسه متحلية بالعمل الذي وعد الله عليه بالثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse exemplifies Quranic mercy expressed through accessible, reassuring meanings that soften hearts.
rows.anchor: وإنما يبعث هذا اللين في القلوب ما في القرآن من معاني الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 43:68–69 exemplify tender meanings that soften believers’ hearts; eloquence has distinct contexts for forceful style and for ease and tenderness.
rows.anchor: وقد علم في فن الخطابة أن للجزالة مقاماتها وللسهولة والرقة مقاماتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran’s wonder is that it produces both fear and desire in the same believers, fitting their conduct to God’s majesty, forbearance, and mercy.
rows.anchor: والمقصود وصفهم بالتأثرين عند تعاقب آيات الرحمة بعد آيات الرهبة

rows.speaker: الفخر
rows.claim: Al-Fakhr quotes perfected seekers: when they encounter divine majesty they are stunned, but when a trace of beauty appears they come alive.
rows.anchor: قال الفخر : إن المحققين من أهل الكمال قالوا : ( السائرون في مبدأ جلال الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two responses are foregrounded here because the verse calls the Quran ‘repeated’; 8:2 mentions believers’ awe at God’s mention, while this passage concerns their response to Quran recitation.
rows.anchor: فالآية هنا ذكرت لهم الحالتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Those that did not die’ coordinates with ‘souls’ under the qualifying sense of ‘at their death’; ‘in their sleep’ attaches to ‘takes,’ describing souls taken nightly and then awakened.
rows.anchor: عطف على الأنفس باعتبار قيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling sleep a taking/death is a linguistic comparison, since ordinary usage does not call a sleeper dead; sleep suspends perception while the main organs remain able to resume their functions on waking.
rows.anchor: وهذا جار على وجه التشبيه بحسب عرف اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in ‘so He retains’ is explicative, bringing out an unstated inference required to explain the taking of souls here.
rows.anchor: لأن ما تقدم يقتضي مقدرا يفصح عنه الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imsāk is holding fast and not releasing; God keeps the soul whose death He decreed and prevents its return, figuratively sustaining the state of death, though the family may wish for revival.
rows.anchor: والإمساك : الشد باليد وعدم تسليم المشدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Irsāl means release and permission to return; ‘the other’ is the soul that did not die, treated as dead in sleep, and God restores its full life, highlighting the difference between the two kinds of taking.
rows.anchor: والإرسال : الإطلاق والتمكين من مبارحة المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘To an appointed term’ modifies ‘sends’; because sending means restoring life, God does not remove that life completely before its divinely assigned term. Tasmiyah means designation, as in 2:282.
rows.anchor: لما فيه من معنى يرد الحياة إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers this reading of the verse as free of strained reinterpretation, ellipsis, or شبه الاستخدام in the phrase about the soul on which death is decreed.
rows.anchor: هذا هو الوجه في تفسير الآية الخلي عن التكلفات

words: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding sentence gives the result of the evidence: death and sleep reveal God’s exclusive control and right to worship; the point is reflection on divine craftsmanship and wisdom encountered daily, not merely distinguishing sleep from death.
rows.anchor: أي أن في حالة الإماتة والإنامة دلائل على انفراد الله تعالى بالتصرف وأنه المستحق للعبادة دون غيره وأن ليس المقصود من هذا الخبر الإخبار باختلاف حالتي الموت والنوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Signs’ is plural because death and sleep are two astonishing states, each involving a different divine act: death removes life and prevents its return; sleep partially withdraws life and repeatedly restores it until permanent removal.
rows.anchor: لأنهما حالتان عجيبتان ثم في كل حالة تصرف يغاير التصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs support both figurative illustration and inference to God’s exclusive control; ‘indeed’ is emphatic because most people act as though they deny the signs by ignoring their implications.
rows.anchor: حاصلة على كل من إرادة التمثيل وإرادة استدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafakkur is effortful thought: sustained mental work and repeated contemplation of how evidence points to truths.
rows.anchor: معالجة الفكر ومعاودة التدبر في دلالة الأدلة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read qaḍā ʿalayhā al-mawt actively, with ‘death’ as its direct object.
rows.anchor: ببناء الفعل للفاعل ونصب الموت

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read the verb passively with ‘death’ nominative, either by deleting the preposition bi- or by construing qaḍā as ‘ordained.’
rows.anchor: ببناء الفعل للنائب وبرفع الموت
